findings.title: queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: The dataclass declares `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`, which Python evaluates once when the class is defined rather than for each AssignmentSource instance. Every source created by from_integration(), and every source reconstructed by from_dict() without an explicit queued value, therefore carries the stale module-import timestamp instead of the time that assignment was queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` if this timestamp is meant to describe an individual assignment.

findings.title: AssignmentSource dictionary does not round-trip queued through the Celery boundary
findings.body: to_dict() returns the queued value as a datetime object, and sync_group_assignee_outbound passes that dictionary as a Celery task argument in sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py. After JSON task serialization the value arrives as a string, while from_dict() constructs AssignmentSource without parsing it back, producing an object whose queued field violates its declared datetime type. Serialize queued as an ISO string and parse it in from_dict(), or remove the unused field before relying on this round-trip.

findings.title: Task passes assignment_source to a method whose abstract contract does not declare it
findings.body: This task now unconditionally calls sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source), even when the value is None, but IssueSyncIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound in sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py does not declare an assignment_source parameter and relies only on implementations accepting **kwargs. The PR instead adds the explicit parameter to the unrelated abstract sync_status_outbound, which this task does not call. An issue-sync implementation with an explicit sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True) signature will raise TypeError on every outbound assignee sync and trigger task retries. Add assignment_source to the sync_assignee_outbound contract and remove or justify the unused change to sync_status_outbound.

findings.title: No test proves non-matching integrations still sync or that deassignment cycles are suppressed
findings.body: The only new outbound test covers assignment when the source integration exactly matches the linked integration. It does not test the stated intended behavior that an assignment originating from one integration still propagates to a different linked integration, nor does it test inbound deassignment with a matching source through GroupAssignee.deassign(). A regression that blocks every non-None AssignmentSource, or that only works for assign=True, would pass the added tests while breaking cross-integration propagation or leaving the deassignment cycle intact.
